question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Ratepayer Protection Act (H R 9340)
plain_language: This bill tells state utility regulators to consider making very large power users, such as data centers using 100 megawatts or more, pay the full extra cost of grid upgrades built to serve them. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Protecting Domestic Mining Act (H R 1501)
plain_language: This bill puts mining infrastructure projects into the FAST Act's faster environmental-review process and blocks a proposed rule that would have limited which mining projects qualify. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

question: On Passage — HEATS Act (H R 5587)
plain_language: This bill exempts certain geothermal activities on state and private lands (except Indian lands) from drilling permit requirements as well as environmental and historic preservation review requirements. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act (H R 4690)
plain_language: This bill repeals certain energy efficiency performance standards for new federal buildings and federal buildings undergoing major renovations. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — To require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend the time period during which licensees are required to commence construction of certain hydropower projects (S 1020)
bill_title: A bill to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend the time period during which licensees are required to commence construction of certain hydropower projects.
plain_language: This bill authorizes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend construction deadlines for hydropower projects that were issued a license before March 13, 2020. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Homeowner Energy Freedom Act (H R 4758)
plain_language: This bill repeals three Department of Energy programs: high-efficiency electric home rebates for certain low- or moderate-income households, state-based home energy efficiency contractor training grants, and assistance for states and localities to adopt specified building energy codes.
